subject: SIG: audit log evidence & export workflow for OrbitSoft
messages:
From: Timothy Huang <tim.huang@orbitsoft.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: OrbitSoft Security <security@orbitsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: follow-up on audit logs evidence and export workflow

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're filling out the SIG questionnaire and have a couple of specific asks under 'Logging & Monitoring' (Control family: Audit & Monitoring):

- Can Redwood provide an artifact that proves event logging is enabled for inference requests (sample events + schema)?
- What is your default retention for audit logs (and can it be extended/preserved for a customer export)?
- Do you support customer-managed exports (S3 push or Kafka/Splunk streaming) or can you provide periodic snapshots?
- For exported logs, how is sensitive data handled (PII redaction or pseudonymization)? We need to demonstrate to our InfoSec that logs we ingest won't contain cleartext customer PII.

We are on a compressed SOC/SIG review timeline and would need evidence (sample files or a short playbook) by end of next week if possible.

Attaching the SIG control checklist where these items are highlighted. Let me know the best way to get you what you need — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Timothy
Security Engineer, OrbitSoft
security@orbitsoft.com

Attachment: orbit_sig_control_list.xlsx (spreadsheet with highlighted controls)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Huang <tim.huang@orbitsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on audit logs evidence and export workflow

Hi Timothy — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the checklist. We're aligned and can provide actionable artifacts. Quick summary of what we can deliver next week: 

1) Sample event export (redacted): JSONL file that contains representative inference-request events and system events (timestamps, request IDs, model variant, latency metrics).
2) Audit log schema CSV and brief README describing each field (attached: redwood_audit_log_schema_v1.csv).
3) Export options doc: steps for a one-off export (presigned S3) and near-real-time streaming to customer endpoints, plus security controls (KMS, IAM).
4) Statement of retention policy (standard: 13 months) and options for customer-initiated preservation/export for longer retention.

A couple of quick clarifications we need from you to tailor the artifacts:
- Do you need streaming (near real-time) into your Splunk/CEF endpoint, or will periodic exports (daily snapshots via S3) suffice?
- Any specific fields you need preserved or removed (e.g., request body, user_email)?

I'll loop in Dev and Rishi for the technical and compliance details — they'll prepare the sample files and an annotated playbook. If you're available Thursday morning we can review the artifacts together.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_audit_log_schema_v1.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Timothy Huang <tim.huang@orbitsoft.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on audit logs evidence and export workflow

Hi all — quick technical note on the exports and redaction options. Posting the short playbook here; I'll attach the actual sample files and presigned-step doc.

Where logs live:
- Inference and control-plane events are written as compressed JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) to our internal object store, which we can export to a customer-specific S3 bucket on request.
- Default retention: 13 months (configurable for Dedicated/Private customers with contract).

Export options we support today:
1) One-off snapshot export: we prepare a range export (time-bounded), redact fields per your spec, and provide a presigned S3 bundle (TLS + presigned URL). Steps documented in s3_presigned_instructions.txt (attached).
2) Streaming: we can stream to a customer Kafka or HTTP collector (mutually authenticated TLS). This is available for Dedicated customers or as a managed integration (security review required).
3) Continuous pull: you can pull from a secure S3 prefix; we rotate short-lived credentials and audit access.

Redaction and PII handling:
- By default, request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model, latency, status codes) are retained in full.
- Payloads that may contain customer PII (e.g., request body fields) are redacted by default in hosted plans. We can provide pseudonymization (deterministic hashing of customer identifiers) if you need linkability without cleartext PII.
- All exports can be encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys (Bring Your Own Key) for S3 at-rest protection.

Evidence we will attach:
- redwood_audit_log_schema_v1.csv (field definitions)
- sample_inference_events_redacted.jsonl (redacted sample, removed request body and hashed user identifiers)
- s3_presigned_instructions.txt (how to download a one-off export)

Next steps:
- Tim: confirm whether you want streaming (Splunk/Kafka) or daily S3 snapshots. If S3, provide preferred bucket/role or we will supply presigned URLs.
- Rishi/Marissa: I'll hand off the export and KMS details to you for the compliance statement.

Thanks,
Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: sample_inference_events_redacted.jsonl, s3_presigned_instructions.txt

From: Timothy Huang <tim.huang@orbitsoft.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: OrbitSoft Security <security@orbitsoft.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on audit logs evidence and export workflow

Thanks Dev — that all looks good and comprehensive. A few follow-ups: 

- Streaming: Prefer to try near-real-time ingestion into our Splunk instance. Can you confirm support for HTTPS collector + mTLS? If not, Kafka is acceptable but we'd prefer HTTPS.
- PII: We need request bodies redacted by default and user identifiers pseudonymized (deterministic hash). Can you confirm determinism so we can join events to our internal transforms?
- Timeline: If you can provide the redacted sample and the presigned download by end of day Friday (2026-09-11), our InfoSec can attach it to the SIG submission.

If all good I can send over an IAM role/bucket details for an S3 staging area as a fallback.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — will keep OrbitSoft Security in the loop.

Best,
Timothy

Attachment: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Huang <tim.huang@orbitsoft.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on audit logs evidence and export workflow

Tim — short confirmation and next steps: 

- Streaming: We support HTTPS collector with mutual TLS for Dedicated or Enterprise-managed integrations. We'll need a short security questionnaire and to set up mTLS cert exchange; I'll have Marissa coordinate that with your security ops.
- Deterministic pseudonymization: confirmed. We use a salted HMAC hash per-customer (salt stored in a KMS-wrapped secret) so joinability is deterministic for your tenant without exposing PII. We'll document the algorithm in the README.
- Timeline: Dev will deliver the redacted sample and S3 presigned instructions by EOD Friday 2026-09-11. Rishi will prepare a short statement of retention policy and an attestation paragraph you can include in the SIG evidence packet.

If you can send the IAM role/bucket details as a fallback, that will speed the one-off export — otherwise we'll stage a presigned bundle.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Friday morning (opt-in) to walk through the artifacts. Thanks for the collaboration.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
